title: Applying pebbledash to an exterior wall
subtitle: Mix and apply a scratch coat, then throw small aggregate onto the wet render to produce a pebbledash exterior finish
excerpt: How to apply pebbledash render to an exterior masonry wall. Covers preparing the surface, applying a scratch coat, throwing aggregate onto the wet render, and allowing to cure.
sourceNotes: Cassell's Cyclopaedia of Mechanics (referenced, not reproduced). Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). City and Guilds plastering practical-skills syllabi (open access).

glossaryTerms.definition: The first coat of render applied to a masonry wall. Applied 10-15 mm thick, then scratched with a comb or scratcher to create a key for the next coat. Also called the undercoat or base coat.

The small stones (typically 6-10 mm washed pea gravel or spar chippings) thrown onto the wet render surface of a pebbledash finish. The aggregate embeds in the surface coat and locks on as the render cures.

A site-mixed or bagged mortar for exterior walls. Typical proportions for a first coat (browning coat): 1 part cement to 4-5 parts sharp sand. Final coat for pebbledash is slightly fatter: 1:3 or 1:4. Additives such as plasticiser are used to improve workability.

content.text: Pebbledash is an exterior render finish: a

thrown onto the wet surface. The aggregate embeds as the render sets. The result is hard-wearing and weather-resistant but unforgiving of poor base preparation.

Check the wall before starting. Sweep a cable-and-pipe detector across the area before any power-tool work. Hack off any loose existing render with a bolster chisel and lump hammer. Wire-brush the exposed masonry to remove dust and loose material. Fill any deep holes or hollow courses with mortar and allow to set before rendering. Dampen the wall with water in the hour before applying the base coat; dry brickwork draws moisture out of the render too fast and weakens the bond.

to a stiff, workable consistency. Load the hawk and apply with the plastering trowel to a depth of 10-15 mm. Work in sections of about 1 square metre at a time. Screed the surface roughly flat with a long straight edge or a plastering rule. Scratch the surface immediately with a devil float or a purpose-made scratcher to leave horizontal or hatched lines about 5 mm deep. This provides the mechanical key for the finish coat. Allow the scratch coat to set for at least 24 hours before continuing.
Apply the finish coat and throw the aggregate

Dampen the scratch coat lightly. Apply the finish coat at 6-10 mm. While the surface is still wet and plastic, throw handfuls of dry aggregate at the wall from a distance of about 500 mm. A cupped-hand throw scatters the stones evenly. Work systematically from the top down so falling excess aggregate does not mark a finished lower section. Press the aggregate gently into the surface with the float face; do not grind it in. The aggregate should be roughly half-embedded in the render.

Keep the new render damp for 3 days by misting lightly in dry weather; never use a full-force hose. Cover with hessian sacking if overnight temperatures are likely to drop below 5 degrees Celsius. Do not paint the render for at least 4 weeks; fresh cement needs to cure fully before it is sealed with masonry paint or sealant.

attrs.symptom: Aggregate falls off in sheets after curing
attrs.cause: The finish coat had begun to skin before the aggregate was thrown, or the aggregate was too wet and did not embed cleanly.
attrs.fix: Hack off the affected area, prepare the base, and relay. Use dry aggregate and throw immediately after applying the finish coat.

attrs.symptom: Deep cracks appear along the joints between new and old render
attrs.cause: Shrinkage at the junction between different render ages or mixes.
attrs.fix: Rake out the crack cleanly, dampen the edges, and fill with a flexible exterior filler or a 1:4 cement-sand mortar pressed in with a trowel.

attrs.symptom: Uneven aggregate coverage with bare patches
attrs.cause: Inconsistent throwing distance or timing (some areas were too far set before the aggregate reached them).
attrs.fix: On a small patch, carefully apply a thin skim of fresh finish coat and rethrow aggregate immediately. Work quickly and blend the edges while both are wet.
